subject: 2000 S Geneva Rd gas-station rezone
comment: My wife and I have owned our home on 322 W 1750 North for the past 20 years. We are deeply opposed to any project on the State Street Corridor at 1600 N. that would affect our traffic (on 400 W or the intersections at 1600 N), parking on 400 W, or the crime rates in this area. We do not think sufficient attention is being given to these factors with the currently proposed apartments at the 1600 N 400 W location. When the State Street Corridor was approved, the incredibly tiny space at that corner was thought small enough that only small businesses or housing could be put in there. We assumed no housing along 400 W could be re-zoned, and certainly no access from 400 W would be granted to any properties there. Now we see that these very things are being considered and we are very upset. There is simply no space for any such building on the corner of 1600 N 400 W if the last house on 400 W remains as currently zoned. We are also deeply concerned about the likelihood of the proposed housing being turned into Section 8 housing before or soon after completion. That seems to be something developers/owners have done in the past in order to get additional credits and other payouts. All in all, this side of the corridor being so close to our homes should not be allowed to have such high-density housing. I recommend that the city council not approve any variances from current zoning at all, and that the city council examine traffic and parking in more detail around such a project. Jason Bench mentioned in a recent meeting that a gas station was once considered for this same space, and the traffic for this new housing project wouldn't be any worse than the gas station. I disagree with that thinking. Gas stations do not attract traffic. They are a stop of convenience for people already leaving or coming through that area. The fact that a gas station was once considered should not be used to justify the traffic and parking problems the proposed building and commercial use would create. In summary, my wife and I are opposed to this project because of the likely traffic, parking, crime impact, and potential for Section 8 approval that would follow. We call on all city council members to change the Corridor Zoning in whatever way necessary to prevent such out-of-place proposals from ever being built so close to single-family residential areas.

subject: North Village District zoning/setbacks
comment: We, the residents of the neighborhood along 400 West adjoining the State Street, North Village District, wish to convey our concerns about the proposed North Village District zone changes. We understand that the fifty-foot setback limiting the height of new developments along 400 West is a positive change to help limit the impact and flow from a commercial area to the residential area. However, we are concerned that not enough is being done to help this problem. The North Orem neighborhoods are much quieter and less commercial than other areas of Orem City, such as the City Center District, the Hub District, The Canyon Crossing District, and even the Arts District Zones. We fear that, as developments begin to build in this area, the quiet, safe neighborhood we love is in jeopardy. Many families have resided in these neighborhoods for decades and include multi-generations from aged parents to small children, for which we have special concerns. Therefore, we are asking that our concerns be considered before any decisions are made. The houses that are currently located in the North Village District that are zoned as NVD-Res(B) and the other homes located along 400 West should be more protected from encroaching developments. We feel the fifty-foot setback that is proposed is insufficient and request it be extended to seventy-five or even 100 feet from 400 West street. This would ensure that we have an adequate buffer in the heights allowed in the edge zone immediately next to our neighborhood. In addition, we feel that these homes located in this North Village District should have the setback for height restrictions measured from their backs and sides of the properties to prohibit excessively high buildings being built directly behind their properties rather than the setback being measured from the curb in front of the property (400 West). We also believe that it would be prudent to change these homes out of the North Village District and back to their original R-zone status to protect the neighborhood from the encroaching businesses and large multifamily developments. We realize that it is sensible for Orem to continue to grow and do not oppose growth itself. However, in this area of Orem we residents encourage growth that does not call for excessively high buildings. We understand that, since the North Village District is the smallest of the state street districts, it does not have a minimum height requirement. On the other hand, we believe that a maximum height limit should be set to prevent these neighborhoods, agreeable blends of well-crafted, established older homes and new homes from being overshadowed by multi-storied, multi-family buildings. We have no problem with State Street and its attendant business and apartment buildings reflecting the vibrant, metropolitan side of Orem City; we just ask the City Planning Commission and other concerned parties to respect and appreciate the value of established, quiet, and safe neighborhoods to the city as well. We also feel the need to address other concerns we have regarding the possibility of a large multi family unit being built in the area of 1600 North and 400 West. Increased traffic in this area is not acceptable. The streets are narrow and the space between State Street and 400 West is so short that if an entrance to a large multifamily development were built, it would create traffic congestion affecting two already busy intersections. The 1600 North corridor is very narrow; traffic moves very fast; and the safety of drivers and pedestrians is of great concern to us. This development could also make turning left onto 400 West from eastbound 1600 North even more difficult considering the fact that 400 West is a collector road that connects to Lindon and Pleasant Grove. It should be noted that we anticipate a substantial increase in traffic resulting from the establishment of a new LDS temple on north 2000 in Lindon. That will be difficult enough, but the increase in congestion as a result of the apartment complex will hardly be tolerable and will be extremely detrimental to our neighborhoods. The surrounding smaller streets, 280 West in particular, would likely see an increase in traffic and congestion issues as well. In addition, potential overflow parking from the project considered would inevitably spread to 400 West. The street is not wide enough to accommodate cars parked along it and would create traffic congestion and safety concerns, particularly in the unfinished portions along the west side. A number of residents who attended previous meetings regarding this project feel that they were misled, and certain requests were disregarded. The State Street Master Plan in 2015 did NOT include the homes in the zoning changes. Open houses and city-held charrettes indicated the zoning for the homes would remain unchanged. Again, this was misled

subject: North Village District zoning/setbacks
comment: My husband and I are highly concerned about the proposed multi-unit apartment building on 1600 N and State bordering 400 W. The parking solutions offered by the builder are not adequate to keep cars off of 400 W and the intersection of 1600 N and State as well as the intersection of 1600 N and 400 W are already very heavy with traffic. How do you plan to keep this district of State street quiet and focused on single family homes as stated in the purposes for the State Street Districts? This area is too small and will be heavily impacted in a negative way if you allow this multi-unit apartment to be built here. Please make the right decision and stop this from moving ahead.

subject: Hillcrest park / greenspace
comment: I was recently made aware of the proposals for the Hillcrest property. I am writing to ask that the city take advantage of this unique opportunity that Orem has to increase our available green space with this piece of land. Please don’t put in more pickle ball courts. The pickle ball courts only appeal to a small percentage of the residents of Orem. It is unfair to take one of the few available spaces left in the city and use it entirely for a small subset of the population, those who would be interested in having enough pickle ball courts for a tournament. Orem needs outside space that will attract kids, tweens, teenagers, and families. We need space that allows outdoor activities for all different age groups. What we need are splash pads and skate parks, a bike track and shade trees, places for picnics and open areas for pick up soccer and football games. Please consider the needs of the entire city when making this decision, and don’t cater to the select few who think that the pickle ball courts we already have all over the city aren’t enough. Please remember all the residents of Orem when deciding what to do with this valuable space. Thank you.

subject: general public comment
comment: Why are the cameras not activated on traffic lights?? The number of people running through red lights are absolutely abhorrent and incredibly dangerous. It causes accidents all the time and there are many near misses. I have watched countless people drive through red lights after pushing the yellow and even plowing through a red light while traffic is moving in the other direction. There was a car that zoomed past me on my way home as I was turning left and they we’re going straight down the canyon, despite their light being red well before and after I turned. I would’ve been blamed if there was an accident! This is a huge problem and I’m tired of it being ignored. Activate the cameras! Issue tickets based on pictures and generate more income. Who do I need to talk to about this and why isn’t it happening already?

subject: Orem Community Park water tank
comment: I want to express my concern about the decision process of the Orem Community Park Water tank. The neighborhood residents and public at large have clearly not been given an opportunity to comment on this massive project. I understand that there is a need to balance cost/disruption/engineering requirements, etc. However, there has been to my knowledge no effort to gather public sentiment prior to making a location decision. Informing us through email on 27 January that an "independent public engagement team" will "gather resident feedback" after the fact, is irresponsible and shows a critical lack of effort to understand the concerns of your citizens. Compare the public input on the $25million library/rec center expansion, with the public input on this $34million dollar project. The lack of public input on the water tank project is overwhelming. Please put a pause on this project so that you can gather the citizen input that you need to make the right decision

subject: general public comment
comment: Having lived in Orem for over 18 years now I want to thank the City of Orem for taking such great care of its properties. They are so well maintained and look so sharp! I have lived, worked, and travelled in so many cities where this isn't the case. So thank you!
